dependency.note: Dependent Grade3proposal including prior reviewed components; not accepted-main or deployment status.

interpretation: Semantic authoring judgments do not certify learner mastery, delivered performance or consumer eligibility. Whole/component, prerequisite and candidate-only support are distinguished. Conditions do not authorize new topics or changes to claims. Later full claims are not lowered from a matching component; existing possible duplicates remain unchanged.

expectations.rationale: Existing investigation/design operations contribute; integrated performance and appropriate equipment/reporting remain.
remainingConditions: Child associations do not automatically certify the overall integrated account.

expectations.rationale: Question selection, close observation, shared fact gathering and evidence-based reporting have existing claims.
remainingConditions: Check an integrated research performance in the science strands; the collection of generic claims is not a completed investigation. Process guidance is flexible by readiness, not a requirement for advanced bibliography or bias analysis in Grade 4.

expectations.rationale: Existing claims cover guided experiments, predictions, recording and conclusions without importing later formal hypothesis/variable terminology.
remainingConditions: A safe, connected performance in relevant science content remains to be demonstrated.

expectations.rationale: Sketches, safe making, motion-design testing and comparisons supply existing engineering operations appropriate to the Grade 4 body content.
remainingConditions: Assess a coherent design/build/test performance, its evidence and response to results; isolated operations are insufficient.
Use readiness-dependent process guidance without requiring every advanced engineering step.

expectations.rationale: The safety and early making claims include hazard-aware plans, safe sensory exploration, careful equipment use and cleanup.
remainingConditions: Explicitly check task-appropriate protective clothing/equipment in addition to general safe handling. Later drilling-specific safeguards do not supply a universal early investigation claim.

expectations.rationale: Scientific reporting and existing vocabulary/audience decisions are reusable.
remainingConditions: Check the actual scientific vocabulary and audience/format choices in a science report; generic vocabulary or writing-process success alone does not certify the integrated requirement.

expectations.rationale: Varied programmed output is present; science-purpose application and technology effects remain.
remainingConditions: Child associations do not automatically certify the overall integrated account.

expectations.rationale: The existing first-program evidence already changes movement, speech and appearance and runs an authored mathematical model. These are real output contributions rather than a new output-programming topic.
remainingConditions: Assess varied output choices for scientific investigations/models and explain the intended purposes. Hardware naming alone is not writing code.

expectations.rationale: Everyday AI examples include benefits and limitations, providing a direct emerging-technology contribution.
remainingConditions: Explain an effect of programmed behaviour as well as an emerging-technology example; device naming alone is insufficient.

deferredCandidates.reason: Broader historical effects can support discussion, but do not themselves explain the role of a programmed instruction.

expectations.rationale: Applications have support; interdisciplinary performance and verified contributions remain.
remainingConditions: Child associations do not automatically certify the overall integrated account.

expectations.rationale: Purposeful products and places, together with property-to-function explanations, support familiar scientific/design applications. Use a relevant example such as a spill-resistant container and its material choice, not an unrelated device list.
Motion-design testing supplies science/data work and shared research supplies information gathering and writing.
remainingConditions: Assess the integrated use of another subject in a real problem; co-listing generic skills is insufficient.

expectations.rationale: Existing biography, community-history and ecological-knowledge claims provide candidates; the resource task does not justify separate community clones.
remainingConditions: Verify age-appropriate resources from multiple communities and examine what the contributions changed.
Do not treat a single biography or a generic ecological statement as complete evidence.

deferredCandidates.reason: One scientific biography is a possible example, not a multi-community review.
Requires factual/cultural and whole-claim review before contextual reuse.
Investigating the importance of a local person or group can support the process, but scientific contributions and multiple communities need verified content.

expectations.rationale: Conservation and species-removal reasoning contribute; perspectives and complete case judgments remain.
remainingConditions: Child associations do not automatically certify the overall integrated account.

expectations.rationale: Harm-reduction explanations and sourced community conservation cases supply contrasting human interventions.
remainingConditions: Compare relevant perspectives and actual positive/negative consequences in a checked habitat/community case. A slogan or a list of actions is insufficient.

expectations.rationale: The diagram claim predicts effects of removal on connected populations; threat knowledge and conservation explanations supply causes and preventive action. Assess the linked ecological consequence and justified protection in a suitable case, rather than just the definition of endangered.
Habitat, feeding relationships, diet and adaptations have support; community definitions and habitat-limit explanations retain explicit conditions.
remainingConditions: Child associations do not automatically certify the overall integrated account.

expectations.rationale: The existing habitat claim explicitly explains provisions and organism interdependence. Use a checked nearby habitat to localize the same knowledge; the location does not require another mastery claim.
Habitat interdependence and varying plant requirements provide real interaction/survival components.
remainingConditions: Make the ecological community account explicit and connect relevant limiting conditions to a local plant-and-animal community. Naming a habitat or one plant need does not establish the whole account.

expectations.rationale: The food-chain claim supplies relationships and predictions, while the vocabulary claim explicitly assesses ecological roles including decomposers. No separate role-naming clone is needed.

The existing representation claim traces multiple chains through a web, identifies shared organisms and predicts changes. This directly supports understanding interconnected chains without requiring authorship of a new web.

deferredCandidates.reason: The later conceptual claim also constructs webs and reasons about population changes. Construction is a distinct operation not made mandatory by this selected expectation; no earlier interval is inferred for the complete later claim.

expectations.rationale: The existing stable claim defines the three diet groups and sorts at least six animals with diet-based reasons. A new age interval associates that same knowledge; it does not create an older version.

The existing broad adaptation claim includes plant and animal examples and survival reasoning; rainforest plant structures supply multiple explicit structural cases. Use a varied set of physical features and their habitat functions.

deferredCandidates.reason: A related existing claim also includes behavioural/physiological examples and natural-selection reasoning. No new structural-adaptation topic or identity change is proposed.

expectations.rationale: Requirements and limited-condition outcomes contribute the resource side of the explanation, so habitat limits are not treated as wholly absent knowledge.
remainingConditions: Explain finite support for the plant-and-animal community, including how available requirements constrain numbers. One deprived plant or a removed food-web node alone is not a general limit explanation.

expectations.rationale: Communication benefits and insect light-disruption cases contribute; full societal/environmental comparisons remain.
remainingConditions: Child associations do not automatically certify the overall integrated account.

expectations.rationale: The existing device-design claim explicitly explains distance communication using light or sound properties.
remainingConditions: Assess actual societal benefits and limitations for suitable devices. Building a working signalling device alone does not establish its wider impacts.

expectations.rationale: The existing insect-conservation claim explicitly names artificial-light disruption of nocturnal insects. This is a substantive environmental effect, not merely a generic pollution prerequisite.
remainingConditions: Compare relevant perspectives and assess sound as well as light cases. A single insect threat does not establish the complete light/sound environmental requirement.

expectations.rationale: Existing sources, biological emission, vibration, material tests and sensory/device claims contribute; complete property/wave/heat contrasts remain.
remainingConditions: Child associations do not automatically certify the overall integrated account.

expectations.rationale: The existing light-source distinction includes Sun, torch and lamp. Assess the natural/artificial classification explicitly; a new source-list topic is unnecessary.

Existing illumination/source distinctions supply objects, while the deep-sea claim explicitly assesses biological light production. Combine those actual claims to distinguish emitted and reflected light, including living cases.
Reflection is explicitly explained and tested; the vocabulary claim explicitly assesses refraction and includes absorption in its full description.
remainingConditions: Demonstrate the straight-path and absorption account; the current vocabulary evidence does not certify every property. Do not infer a complete ray model from a shadow alone.

deferredCandidates.reason: The complete later claim begins at10 and includes straight-line explanation and ray diagrams; it is not lowered from one matching clause.
The complete later reflection/refraction claim is not lowered for the earlier named property.

expectations.rationale: Medium propagation, echoes and changed vibrations have existing assessed support. The wave vocabulary description also includes absorption.
remainingConditions: Assess the wave-travel and absorption explanation explicitly. Naming wavelength or hearing an echo does not itself show the whole account.

deferredCandidates.reason: The complete later claim includes longitudinal pressure waves, compression/rarefaction and speed comparisons; no9–10context is inferred solely from its overlapping clauses.

expectations.rationale: Existing evidence demonstrates vibrating sources and propagation through materials, rather than treating sound generation as absent.
remainingConditions: Connect the vibrating source to the travelling wave explicitly; a moving rubber band alone is not the full wave explanation.

deferredCandidates.reason: The later complete pressure-wave claim is retained unchanged and not lowered for a simpler sound-production component.

expectations.rationale: Existing material tests compare light transmission/blocking and reflection, while medium examples explain sound travel through solids, liquids and gas. Use varied objects and materials in the combined task rather than accepting one torch test.
The Sun claim explicitly supplies joint light/heat output, and energy vocabulary supplies transfers in familiar devices.
remainingConditions: Provide and assess checked low-heat light examples and the contrast. Ordinary device naming is not evidence that all its output is light, or that a source produces zero heat.

expectations.rationale: The senses and eye claims supply sensory identification and light reception; the computer-component claim explicitly identifies cameras, microphones, screens and speakers and chooses components by purpose. Inner-ear anatomy is not made an additional requirement.
Mechanism utility and environmental design factors contribute; complete community and same-purpose comparisons remain.
remainingConditions: Child associations do not automatically certify the overall integrated account.

expectations.rationale: Existing everyday mechanism functions and user-purpose explanations supply direct benefit/use components.
remainingConditions: Assess actual effects in more than one community setting. A useful lever example does not itself establish social comparisons or drawbacks.

expectations.rationale: Design-factor trade-offs explicitly include sustainability; resource knowledge explicitly connects fuel extraction/use to environmental effects.
remainingConditions: Compare checked machines that perform a similar purpose and justify their environmental differences. Neither a generic sustainability word nor fuel naming alone completes the comparison.

expectations.rationale: Everyday functions and force changes have support; complete component and kinematic accounts retain conditions.
remainingConditions: Child associations do not automatically certify the overall integrated account.

expectations.rationale: The existing mechanism claim uses everyday seesaw, flagpole and bicycle cases and explains what their mechanisms accomplish. No separate machine-list claim is needed.
The existing lever evidence explicitly names effort, load and pivot and relates their roles; pulley and gear functions are also present.
remainingConditions: Assess identified component roles across varied mechanisms. A whole-device purpose or a lever-only part list does not establish each selected mechanism part.

expectations.rationale: Gear and pulley transfer explanations supply a direct component beyond generic pushes and pulls.
remainingConditions: Make the transferred motion types, including rotation, explicit across selected systems. Force transfer does not automatically demonstrate every motion-transmission description.

expectations.rationale: The existing gears/pulleys claim explicitly changes force direction and effect; it supplies relevant mechanism knowledge.
remainingConditions: Show the actual motion transformations, including change of geometric plane and speed/direction in suitable mechanisms. A smaller effort is not interchangeable with every kinematic explanation.

expectations.rationale: The complete existing claim explicitly compares lever, pulley and gear force effects. No extra older-grade force-change topic or quantitative mechanical-advantage calculation is imposed.
Process effects and material uses contribute; full life-cycle/perspective cases remain.
remainingConditions: Child associations do not automatically certify the overall integrated account.

expectations.rationale: Earthquake cause/surface effects, protective design and erosion prevention supply substantive process-consequence and response components.
remainingConditions: Analyse checked societal and environmental consequences; a description of shaking or protective device alone does not complete both sides.

expectations.rationale: Material uses, extraction/fuel environmental effects and recycling solutions contribute real stages of the resource account.
remainingConditions: Assess the complete selected material life-cycle case, its social/environmental trade-offs and relevant perspectives. Mineral naming or generic recycling does not certify all stages.

deferredCandidates.reason: The full later resource/circular-economy claim is not assigned an earlier interval solely for an extraction or recycling clause.

expectations.rationale: Rock cycle, property observations, uses and fossil inference have support; composition classification and verified community knowledges remain.
remainingConditions: Child associations do not automatically certify the overall integrated account.

expectations.rationale: The existing cycle claim traces a complete pathway through weathering, sediment formation, pressure, heat and melting and explains changes among rock types. Its complete assessed operation matches this expectation; no age-specific rock-cycle clone is created.

deferredCandidates.reason: A parallel existing record has substantially overlapping full-cycle evidence and additional sample/geological-time examples. This is an existing-ID duplication-review candidate, not a reason to add or reshape topics during alignment.

expectations.rationale: Rock observation/grouping explicitly tests texture, hardness, grain size and colour; the existing type claim supplies the classification. Describe checked specimens from each type without claiming a universal colour or hardness for an entire class.
Existing rock grouping and mineral colour/lustre/scratch-hardness testing already assess multiple physical criteria.
remainingConditions: Verify the composition-based classifications as well as physical tests. Observable colour or a rock-type label alone does not establish mineral composition.

expectations.rationale: The existing resource claim directly matches clay/bricks, sand/glass, ore/metal and salt/use cases. Generic material-use knowledge contributes without relabelling its Australian case evidence as Indigenous Ontario knowledge.
Existing burial/preservation knowledge and inferences from fossils about former organisms/environments jointly support the complete requirement. Similar fossil titles do not warrant another topic.

deferredCandidates.reason: A related existing record focuses on patterns in strata and landscape change, a distinct inference operation; not automatically added as a duplicate of basic formation.

expectations.rationale: Generic mineral properties and use reasoning exist, but they do not establish the named community knowledges. The missing culturally verified cases are retained explicitly rather than invented or relabelled.
remainingConditions: Use appropriate authoritative community sources and assess the knowledge/property/purpose connection. A generic scratch test or a community-identity lesson alone cannot satisfy the expectation.

deferredCandidates.reason: Material selection/use knowledge is available for a carefully sourced task but currently has no verified complete community-specific case set.
